output.name: Sekál — The Bone Gull
output.myth: When Ennu had no more nets to mend, he took the jawbone of a whale that Orrun had cast onto the north shore and carved a gull from it. Short neck, round body. He cut its wings from goat-hide, stretched and smoked until it stopped smelling of goat. Then he sang to it, which is the only way to make a thing fly. The gull lifted off the rock when he let go. Hesk, who winds every string at the pole, heard it pass and asked it for the names. The gull could not speak, so it flew, and the wind carried each name up the line into Hesk's reel. Tavo tried to tear its wings once, laughing, and failed. Above it, the Gull Who Waited keeps its eye on the bone gull from the north, so someone could be seen from Vel. Off to the south-west the red Hanging Hawk hangs on its line and sulks, never having flapped. Your grandfather's name is in there somewhere, if the wind was kind. Go and ask Hesk, but keep your hands off the line.
output.finding: Find the Gull Who Waited high in the north, then look a little under a hand-span (about 16°) straight south of it to find the Bone Gull.
